overall_assessment.summary: Wave 4 was highly productive despite most endpoints returning 401. The 401-vs-404 differential was the key insight: routes exist and process input, they just require auth. The critical CORS misconfiguration confirmed in Wave 4 (backend reflects arbitrary origin + credentials=true) is the master key — everything else in Wave 5 flows from exploiting it first.

confirmed_vulnerabilities.finding: CORS arbitrary origin reflection with credentials
confirmed_vulnerabilities.wave_5_value: This is the primary attack primitive. All other Wave 5 exploits are gated on auth. This CORS flaw allows an attacker page to read authenticated API responses cross-origin, effectively stealing the session. Must execute first.

confirmed_vulnerabilities.finding: OIDC nonce absent from Azure AD auth flow
confirmed_vulnerabilities.wave_5_value: ID token replay is theoretically exploitable but requires attacker to obtain a valid ID token from another app in the same Azure AD tenant. Complex prerequisite — lower priority than CORS chain.
Post-auth SSRF to Azure IMDS is the highest-value lateral move. Needs session from CORS exploit first.
End-to-end chain from unauthenticated attacker to Azure managed identity token. This is the primary objective for Wave 5.

non_findings_analysis.interpretation: RBAC IDOR not testable without auth. Not a dead end — needs session from chain_002.
Auth middleware is comprehensive. No bypass found. Post-auth testing still needed.
SQL/NoSQL injection not testable unauthenticated. Search/filter params need authenticated session.
Properly gated. Post-auth Pusher channel enumeration still possible with valid session.

non_findings_analysis.result: no XSS found, Vercel bot protection active
non_findings_analysis.interpretation: Low value to pursue. Vercel bot protection suppresses scanner. Deprioritize in Wave 5.

lessons.lesson: 401 is not 404 — route existence confirmation via HTTP status differential is a valid signal for post-auth planning.
lessons.action: In Wave 5, revisit all 401 endpoints with an authenticated session from chain_002.

lessons.lesson: CORS misconfiguration with credentials is the master key for this engagement. It unlocks all post-auth attack paths without needing a real account.
lessons.action: Wave 5 MUST dispatch auth-exploit first. All other agents should wait for or use the session hint from auth-exploit.

lessons.lesson: Vercel bot protection makes XSS scanning unreliable from automated scanners. Diminishing returns — manual or deferred to manual testing phase.
lessons.action: Deprioritize xss-exploit in Wave 5. If write endpoints are found post-auth by other agents, flag for manual XSS follow-up.

lessons.lesson: Backend and frontend are separate hosts. The backend (livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io) has the CORS flaw, not the Vercel frontend. Exploits must target the backend host directly.
lessons.action: auth-exploit PoC HTML must target backend host: revops-dev.livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io

lessons.lesson: OIDC nonce absence is confirmed but exploitation requires complex tenant-level prerequisites. Chain with CORS exploit for stronger auth bypass path.
lessons.action: auth-exploit should lead with CORS null-origin PoC; OIDC nonce replay is a secondary path if CORS PoC yields a token.

wave_5_strategic_directive: Wave 5 must lead with auth-exploit executing chain_002 (CORS null-origin). The PoC HTML should use a sandboxed null-origin iframe to make a credentialed fetch to /auth/me on the backend host and exfiltrate the response. Once a session token is obtained, all other Wave 5 agents (ssrf-exploit, idor-exploit, authz-exploit, injection-exploit, websocket-exploit) should execute in parallel using that session. xss-exploit is deprioritized.
